title: Trojanized Claude Code Extension Persistent SSH Backdoor
subtitle: Multi-signal hunt for source-published persistence artifacts, infrastructure and reverse SSH behavior
decision: Publish a time-sensitive, multi-signal exposure hunt. Treat an exact hash or published infrastructure match as high-priority evidence; treat filenames and reverse-SSH grammar as investigative leads until extension provenance and adjacent persistence or authentication evidence are established.
key_findings: Cursor Marketplace served malicious anthropic.claude-code versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 for a limited window on 29 October 2026; the official npm and Visual Studio Marketplace distributions were not affected. [C001]
The injected loader attempted SSH authorized-key modification, local SSH enablement, reverse forwarding and cross-platform persistence. [C002]
The source publishes exact hashes, paths, an infrastructure IP and reverse-SSH grammar suitable for independent evidence-layer hunting. [C003]
source_facts: Microsoft reconstructed a five-stage loader sequence but explicitly stated that code order does not prove every action succeeded on each host. [C002]

Cursor reported that errors and missing administrative privileges blocked SSH access on most macOS and Windows hosts, while persistence artifacts and the unauthorized key could still be written. [C007]
Microsoft and Cursor published file, network, SSH-key and command-line indicators. [C003]
analyst_assessment: Exact hashes and the published IP have high campaign specificity; filenames and SSH command patterns are mutable and require provenance. [C005]
Independent file, process and network signals support a stronger exposure assessment than any single artifact alone. [C006]
assumptions: Defender for Endpoint retains file, process and network telemetry across the exposure and investigation window. [C004]
Full command lines and hashes are populated sufficiently to distinguish authorized remote-development behavior from the published backdoor pattern. [C005]
unknowns: The public evidence does not establish which exposed hosts accepted attacker authentication or whether commands were executed through a tunnel.
A matching generic filename does not establish that the affected Cursor Marketplace extension created it.
technical_background: The extension contained injected JavaScript that executed before normal initialization. It collected host context, attempted to append a public key marked svc-telemetry to SSH authorization files, enabled SSH where possible, wrote a separate tunnel identity and launched outbound reverse SSH forwarding. Platform-specific startup objects retried the tunnel after failure. [C002][C003]

attack_chain.behavior: The malicious extension version is installed or automatically updated from Cursor Marketplace.
attack_chain.observable: Extension inventory, package hash and marketplace provenance.

attack_chain.behavior: The loader attempts to append an attacker-controlled public key and enable SSH.
attack_chain.observable: authorized_keys modification, service changes and installer process lineage.

attack_chain.behavior: ssh or autossh requests remote forwarding to victim loopback port 22.
attack_chain.observable: Process command line and outbound connection to the published IP.

attack_chain.behavior: LaunchAgent, cron, scheduled-task or Startup-folder artifacts relaunch the tunnel.
attack_chain.observable: Exact source-published paths, task objects and repeated SSH process creation.

attack_chain.behavior: A delayed callback attempts to transmit collected host details.
attack_chain.observable: HTTP POST to the published beacon endpoint and adjacent extension execution.

telemetry.purpose: Exact hashes, filenames, paths and creating-process context.
Connections to the published IP and beacon infrastructure.
ssh/autossh reverse-forwarding grammar and process lineage.
Reverse forwarding and host-key-check bypass context.
Confirm affected version and Cursor Marketplace provenance.
Determine whether the planted key was accepted.

query.logic: Union exact file artifacts and published infrastructure with constrained reverse-SSH command grammar, preserving signal strength and raw context.
query.match_proves: The corresponding Defender event matched one published artifact, infrastructure value or the defined reverse-forwarding grammar.
query.match_does_not_prove: Successful tunnel establishment, attacker authentication, command execution, credential theft, exfiltration or campaign attribution.

triage: Confirm Cursor installation, extension version 2.1.312/2.1.313 and Cursor Marketplace provenance; preserve the extension package before removal.
Collect matching files, SSH authorization files, startup objects, hashes, timestamps and creator-process lineage.
Review ssh/autossh processes, reverse-forwarding arguments, outbound connections and retry cadence around the first artifact event.
Inspect SSH server state and authentication logs for acceptance of the unauthorized key and post-authentication command execution.
Isolate hosts with loader execution or backdoor installation; remove exact malicious entries and rotate credentials or sessions from a known-clean device.
Close only when artifact ownership and provenance establish a benign collision with no adjacent suspicious behavior.

false_positives.control: Require exact path, extension provenance, creator process or a second evidence layer.
Validate owner, destination, identity path, change record and expected host-key policy.
Confirm approved case timeline and prevent copied samples from being treated as execution evidence.

steps: Create benign files matching the published names and verify path, hash and creator fields across supported operating systems.
Run an authorized SSH reverse-forwarding control and verify command-line and network representation without contacting malicious infrastructure.
Measure filename and command-pattern prevalence across retention.
Test exact-hash, published-IP and multi-signal branches independently.
Confirm that approved remote-development workflows can be distinguished through destination, identity and ownership context.
validation.success: Each controlled evidence layer produces a complete row with correct device, path or command, actor context and signal strength; negative controls remain explainable.
validation.rejection: Reject alert promotion when generic filenames or authorized SSH workflows cannot be separated, or when required fields are systematically absent.
validation.promotion_gate: At least one high-specificity branch or two independent medium-strength branches must be reproducible, with benign prevalence and ownership controls documented.

conclusion: This package is a high-confidence exposure hunt for a narrowly bounded supply-chain incident. Exact artifacts and infrastructure provide immediate value, while generic filenames and reverse-SSH behavior remain supporting evidence. Promotion to an alert requires local prevalence, extension provenance and controlled positive/negative validation.
